title: The Lady of A Thousand Swords

content.text:
## The Lady of a Thousand Swords

_<font face="Times New Roman">"It is the pain itself that protects me."</font>_

I _still_ want to paint this piece as a massive mural down in Deep Ellum -- that hidden-away barrio of street art in central Dallas. It's no secret that the design was heavily inspired by the Lady of Pain from the _Forgotten Realms_ mythos. "The Lady of a Thousand Swords" has become one of my most popular designs of all time. In fact, both me and my brother Skybreak are still rocking her on our phone cases.

The Lady of a Thousand Swords wears a war bonnet forged of serrated metal fractal feathers. It's a bladed crown that continuously cuts into her, serving as her own source of pain even as it violently protects her from the outside world. Those intricate, digital fractal feathers fan outward, forming a chaotic halo all around her. And the world? It never gets to see the gaze that would assuredly entomb the beholder in a grave of eternal stone.

And yeah... you might as well consider this painting a direct commentary on my love life and the incredible, chaotic train wrecks I tend to be attracted to. _I'll own up to that._

While you can grab prints and some other killer merch [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/i/notebook/The-Lady-of-a-Thousand-Swords-Desert-Tribal-Fractal-Fusion-by-jayaprime/39758392/qhru), the custom Otterbox cases are a different beast. They aren't cheap, so you'll need to [hit me up directly](contact). Just shoot me a message with the exact make and model of that supercomputer hiding in your pocket... I'll give you a ring, ding, ding!

My "1000 Swords" design is part of the greater Urban Geometry series that I ran crossing over from summer of 2019 right into autumn, befitting of the faded colors. I loved working with so many different artists and models on the series, bringing in heavy elements from street art and tattoo culture, merging them in with different fractal designs as part of the paintings. Rather fitting for my roots in [the adHF](adhd-revolution).

texts: "For even in the dawning dreams of spring are ever-woven the final falling leaves of autumn."

## The Geometer + The Secret of the Sphinx

From the Urban Geometry series, three pieces have become my own personal favorites. You've seen "1000 Swords", there's also "[May Angels Take You](may-angels-take-you)", then there's this one that is near and dear to my heart. I worked with the incredible Alessandra Vela herself ([Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/ArtbyAlessandra1)) on this one. Alessandra is an artist who's absolutely exploding with creativity, whether that's painting, videography, or my own personal favorite -- makeup design! She uses makeup to create optical illusions, unique characters, and completely transform herself. To take this to the next level, she then creates videos depicting these along with photos, both of which require their own level of unique artistry.

To say I'm honored to have worked with her on "The Geometer" is to make a grievous understatement.

Working with her on this left me obsessed with the concept of the body itself as separate, yet unified parts and how they connect to The Ship of Theseus itself (aka, "Theseus's Paradox"; [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_of_Theseus)). So using the same techniques, I returned to the concept, quite literally using the painting and design process to learn, explore, and come to know each concept on an intimate, personal level.

How many pieces can we remove from ourselves before we're no longer there?

I came to understand that we are not our parts, and not the sum of our parts, but instead something deeper that emerges from within these broken pieces... a "haunting" or "poltergeist" behind the anima of the objects themselves.. . each its own useful tool at the hands of the driver.

These are the true secrets and hidden treasures of the sphinx herself.

## Extended Exploration

If you like these pieces from the Urban Geometry series, then you've got to check out my "[May Angels Take You](may-angels-take-you)" design! I also have a whole collection of [pop art fractals](other-pop-art) to explore. For those who love these autumn sunset colors, my surreal "[Ship for All Destinations](destination-everywhere)" collaboration with my master Batoruco will call you out to sea with it.
